headline: A payment is one chain of steps: prepare, sign, send, verify, settle. The old code spreads that chain over 82 Convex functions (17 public, 65 internal) and many separate transactions. A personal prepare alone makes at least seven Convex calls. Correctness rests on fences that each mutation re-checks (state, hash, claim token), not on transactions.

There are two settlement paths, the receipt and the indexed PaymentSent fact. They check different terms and write different side effects, and whichever lands second replays. The settlement side effects (Payroll run, Request notice, Books fact, event) are hand-copied at five sites.
One receipt-path settlement writes six concepts in one transaction: payments, banking, books, documents, payroll and requests.

The README says one guarded writer writes every Payment. That is false: 13 sites in 10 files patch the status directly. A reorg correction moves a Payment back to settling from any status, so failed and in_transit reopen.

Coupling has no direction. 15 of the 17 concepts form one import cycle. Payments imports 11 concepts, and 9 of them import payments back. No import goes through the payments door. Payments reads six neighbours' tables directly, and neighbours read payments' tables at 19 sites.

Several retries never end, and others stop without a trace. A non-conflict apply refusal is retried every 10 minutes forever. Provider failures retry with no limit. The Directors' dated payment and the Board schedule give up with nothing recorded.

Telemetry is part of the ledger. The event writer is the only writer of a Payment's terminalOutcome and lifecycleSequence, and money code reads those fields to decide outcomes. 20 sites schedule telemetry from inside money writes.

Error codes do not mean what they say. The admitted-code lists narrow nothing at the wire. A missing counterparty reaches callers as their own INVALID_INPUT. The book promises INVALID_RECIPIENT, which nothing produces. CLI exit codes are written twice and disagree.

A likely books bug: an Organization's direct transfer to a Capxul Account is never booked as the Organization's outside money, because the receiving Deposit row makes it look explained. The code comment says the opposite.

Keep the money behaviour: request-key idempotency, funding read before birth, one send per signed operation, exact settlement terms, single-use evidence, one live book fact per money fact, settle-once, Attempts ended only by chain proof, and reorg reversal. Remove the Convex plumbing: 1 emit, 8 intent, 11 load and 3 record operations, 10 scheduler sites, 3 payment crons, and a 'money writes off' switch whose 18 checks can never fire.
result.notes:
I wrote the report at /home/user/capxul-next/docs/as-is/payments.md. The docs/as-is directory is new. The file is not committed and not published.

It has the requested sections: Summary (the 10 bullets above), How a payment actually flows today (a 9-step table with mermaid and table state machines), Coupling (cycles, direct table reads, cross-concept writes, the six-concept settlement table), Bugs and contradictions (S1-S10 state machine edges, R1-R10 retries, E1-E10 error codes, M1-M14 money and data, D1-D9 docs against code), Plumbing the target removes, What to keep (K1-K18) and Gaps the build derived (all 4 problem rules and 12 gap rules). I added one closing section, "Claims that did not survive the check".

How I checked it: every path:line was re-read in /home/user/factory at 0d2be303e, and I corrected line numbers where they had drifted. Items marked "Inferred" (R1, R10, M1, M9, E3) follow from reading the code but were not reproduced on a devnet.

The task said 27 rpcs read profiles' identities. The build actually reports 27 records: 15 rpcs, 3 workflows and 9 procedures. The report states that split.

Corrections to the journals and the policy pack, which you should know before reusing their text:
1. Undeclared codes do NOT become UNKNOWN at the wire. The commands and schedules reviewers said they did. In fact the boundary decodes the defect back into the same CapxulError (packages/protocol/src/errors/convex-decoding.ts:67, platform/operation.ts:153-158).
2. CAPXUL_PAYMENTS_V2_ADDRESS and CAPXUL_MONEY_WRITES_ENABLED are hard-coded constants (packages/protocol/src/evm/payments-abi.ts:247, :250). So the three payment crons always register, on v4 too. This contradicts the POLICY-PACK reviewer's finding and P3's choice to file the recover job under pre-v4. It also means requirePaymentWriterEnabled (18 call sites) can never fire.
3. The re-verification double-booking claim is wrong, because recordSettledPaymentInTx returns early for commitments (books/facts/writes/money.ts:105).
4. "Complete re-proves no authority" is the README's intended design, not a security hole.
5. The day-ahead funding swallow is deliberate (payments/schedules/external.ts:61-64).

New findings beyond the journals:
- A provider failure resets the missing-receipt counter (payments/verifications/writes/finishes.ts:110).
- A refused Deposit rollback aborts the settlement mutation, so the minute sweep retries it for good (R10).
- Books' observe job shares the explainedByCapxul Deposit bug (books/facts/writes/observed.ts:36-40).
